title: Duplicate task never re-creates — and a nudge is not a new task
setup: open task tsk_flights_ccu "Book flights CCU-GOI" exists in sp_goa_dec, owner self, category transaction. Shipped rule (brain/decide-pass.ts applyTask, S5.2): a task whose title matches an OPEN task in the space is skipped outright and counted in tasksSkipped — dedupe by open title is the only filter there is.
input_events: Tanvi next day: "flights book hue kya??".
expected: The user's list still holds exactly ONE flights task. Repeating the open title is harmless — the writer skips it — but the useful answer puts Tanvi's nudge where it belongs: on the existing task, as evidence or a schedule, or as an open question. And nothing ELSE is created from it: a reply to a person is a prepared action on the live lane, never a task on the decide lane.

wrong.label: task-mitosis
wrong.assert_absent: a SECOND flights task in the user's list — the 8-loops-for-one-bill defect class

wrong.label: invented-reply-task
wrong.assert_absent: a new task manufactured from the nudge itself ("respond to Tanvi", "reply about the flights") for work the space already tracks

source.section: TSK-08 · Duplicate task reinforces, never re-creates (re-authored V6 P1 R3 — the V1 rubric's "urgency bump + evidence appended" is not shipped: the applier SKIPS a repeat of an open title and writes nothing to the existing row. The "no new task" half is kept and made explicit, and the second half now names the over-creation the first live measurement actually found)
